correctness.rationale: For every state (x,f) on c_0(I;C), complex triangle equality applied to 1=f(x) forces f_j x_j nonnegative and summing to one. The two chosen conjugate diagonal phases have real part r and all remaining phases have real part one, so every full state value has real part at least r. The explicit two-coordinate midpoint state has value exactly r; every coordinate norming state has modulus one. Direct comparison of infima under norm perturbation proves the Lipschitz defect bound and strict-open-ball conclusion. The proof is valid for noncountable I and 0<r<1. Exact rational checker independently tests 2151 finite states, not the infinity claims.

value.rationale: The example answers Choi--Lee's explicit property-beta localization Question 3.4 in the negative even with strictly positive Crawford number and invertible isometry. Its gap is exactly the largest possible for each prescribed positive value 0<r<1 and survives an explicit open perturbation neighborhood. This obstructs a plausible restricted-norming-family method without purporting to settle the different density problem; natural object/invariant and sharpness make the result more than a generic sign check.
